takeaways.statement: Avoid pre-shredded cheese because it contains anti-caking agents that prevent it from melting properly.
A Baking Steel is the key to achieving a crispy 'undercarriage' or bottom crust in a home oven.
Preheat your home oven to its maximum temperature (550°F) for at least one hour before baking.
Use semolina flour on the pizza peel to prevent the dough from sticking.

items.name: Sauce Preparation
items.details: Mix Mutti Passata with salt, oregano, and pepper. Optional: fresh garlic, olive oil, and basil.

items.name: Cheese Preparation
items.details: Grate whole milk low moisture mozzarella. Can mix with Edam for better browning.

items.name: Oven Setup
items.details: Place Baking Steel in oven. Preheat to 550°F for 1 hour.

items.name: Dough Handling
items.details: Remove dough from fridge 2-3 hours before use. Dust peel with semolina. Stretch using knuckle-to-knuckle method.

parsed_output.embedding_text: A detailed home pizza-making tutorial by creator AJ (@ajeatworld) focusing on the best ingredients and equipment for a professional-style thin crust. The video provides specific recommendations for tomato sauces, including Bianco DiNapoli Whole Peeled Tomatoes, Cento San Marzano, and Mutti Passata. AJ demonstrates the importance of using Trader Joe's Whole Milk Low Moisture Mozzarella and grating it fresh to avoid anti-caking agents. Essential equipment highlighted includes the Baking Steel for achieving a crispy crust in a standard Hotpoint oven at 550°F, along with a pizza peel and infrared thermometer. The guide covers technical steps like dusting the peel with King Arthur Semolina flour and the 'knuckle to knuckle' dough stretching technique. This part two video is designed for home cooks looking to elevate their pizza game through specific product choices and professional methods.
